chunks: And Moses felt afraid within himself.

key_terms.أَوْجَسَ: felt a sudden fear or apprehension

ai.seo_question: What did Moses feel in his heart when confronting Pharaoh?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the concept of *al-waqar* (dignified composure) and the natural human emotion (*fitrah*) of the prophets, distinguishing their momentary apprehension from weakness. It underscores Moses' (AS) reliance on divine support when facing the tyrant Pharaoh, serving as a model for believers in maintaining spiritual resilience during trials. This moment precedes his declaration of trust in God, illustrating the transition from internal fear to outward confidence through divine aid.
